Links: [{"title":"leakguard 0.5.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/latest/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"ci: redact organization names, internal hosts, emails, and secrets in triaged issues by kolatts · Pull Request #504 · kolatts/pncli · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/kolatts/pncli/pull/504"},{"title":"GitHub - sumankrsh/local-redact: Redact sensitive data before you paste it into an LLM. Runs in your browser; checksum-checked Gulf and Indian IDs. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/sumankrsh/local-redact"},{"title":"leakguard 0.1.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.1.0/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"leakguard 0.2.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.2.0/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs"},{"title":"cleansh 0.1.4","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/cleansh/0.1.4/source/src/main.rs"},{"title":"GitHub - happygream/hexredact: Heavy, reversible redaction of PII, secrets and infrastructure identifiers in log files. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/happygream/hexredact"},{"title":"leakguard 0.1.2","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/0.1.2/source/tests/integration.rs"},{"title":"GitHub - rog7/redact: Hide emails, API keys, and tokens in a log before you share it. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/rog7/redact"},{"title":"Crate cleansh","url":"https://docs.rs/cleansh/0.1.7/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/cleansh/"}]

Several open-source CLIs match this description. I haven't checked their licenses or maintenance status, so verify those before using one.

- **leakguard** (Rust): It redacts secrets and PII, including emails, IPs, JWTs, and API keys, from stdin or files to stdout. A `--check` flag exits non-zero when sensitive data is found. The docs show `tail -f app.log | leakguard` as an example. Fast, zero-dependency redaction of secrets and PII (emails, credit cards, IPs, JWTs, API keys, and more) from text and logs.
- **local-redact** (Python): It covers emails, IPs, API keys, and several regional ID types. It reads stdin and writes stdout, and it has a JSON report and an allowlist. Its README lists cat app.log | local-redact redact > app.redacted.log          # stdin to stdout as a usage example.
- **hexredact**: This tool does reversible redaction through a mapping file, so the same value always gets the same token. It reads stdin when given `-`. UI output goes to stderr, so stdout carries only the redacted text.
- **cleansh** (Rust): It targets terminal output and masks emails, IPs, and tokens such as JWTs and AWS keys. Piped directly from stdin or loaded from files, cleansh provides a robust, pre‑configured solution for data sanitization.
- **rog7/redact** (Python): This is a simpler option for emails, API keys, and tokens. The cleaned log is printed to stdout. The original file is not changed.

For a reversible mapping, hexredact or local-redact fit best. For a simple stdin-to-stdout filter with a CI-friendly check, leakguard fits best.

GitHub - sumankrsh/local-redact: Redact sensitive data before you paste it into an LLM. Runs in your browser; checksum-checked Gulf and Indian IDs. · GitHub
GitHub - happygream/hexredact: Heavy, reversible redaction of PII, secrets and infrastructure identifiers in log files. · GitHub

results:
Several open-source CLIs match this description. I haven't checked their licenses or maintenance status, so verify those before using one.

- **leakguard** (Rust): It redacts secrets and PII, including emails, IPs, JWTs, and API keys, from stdin or files to stdout. A `--check` flag exits non-zero when sensitive data is found. The docs show `tail -f app.log | leakguard` as an example. Fast, zero-dependency redaction of secrets and PII (emails, credit cards, IPs, JWTs, API keys, and more) from text and logs.
- **local-redact** (Python): It covers emails, IPs, API keys, and several regional ID types. It reads stdin and writes stdout, and it has a JSON report and an allowlist. Its README lists cat app.log | local-redact redact > app.redacted.log          # stdin to stdout as a usage example.
- **hexredact**: This tool does reversible redaction through a mapping file, so the same value always gets the same token. It reads stdin when given `-`. UI output goes to stderr, so stdout carries only the redacted text.
- **cleansh** (Rust): It targets terminal output and masks emails, IPs, and tokens such as JWTs and AWS keys. Piped directly from stdin or loaded from files, cleansh provides a robust, pre‑configured solution for data sanitization.
- **rog7/redact** (Python): This is a simpler option for emails, API keys, and tokens. The cleaned log is printed to stdout. The original file is not changed.

For a reversible mapping, hexredact or local-redact fit best. For a simple stdin-to-stdout filter with a CI-friendly check, leakguard fits best.

content.content:
**leakguard 1.0.0** (released 2026-10-06)

- **License:** Dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option.
- **Repository:** https://github.com/ptukovar/leakguard
- **Install:**
  - CLI: `cargo install leakguard`
  - Library: add `leakguard = "1.0.0"` to `[dependencies]`

**CLI examples**
- Pipe a live log: `tail -f app.log | leakguard`
- Keep the last 4 characters: `leakguard --mask partial --keep 4 access.log > clean.log`
- Custom template: `leakguard --mask template --template "<{LABEL}>" access.log`
- Allowlist values: `leakguard --ignore 10.0.0.1,test@example.com app.log`
- Redact custom terms: `leakguard --redact-word AcmeCorp --redact-literal "CUST-9981:CUSTOMER" app.log`
- Limit detectors: `leakguard --only email,ipv4 --mask char --char '#'` or `--without phone`
- Print statistics: `leakguard --stats app.log`
- NDJSON output: `leakguard --json`, with `--show-values` to include matched text
- List detector names: `leakguard --list-kinds`

**Flags and exit codes**
- `--check` fails the build when it finds a match. `--verbose` prints kinds, offsets, and line/column to stderr.
- Exit status is 0 for success (including no findings under `--check`), 1 when `--check` finds a match, and 2 for usage or I/O errors.

**Detected patterns**
- Enabled by default: email, credit card (Luhn-validated), IPv4, IPv6, JWT, US SSN, MAC address, AWS access key, URL credentials, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Google API, OpenAI, PEM private key, IBAN (mod-97 validated), Azure storage connection string, Telegram bot token, and Discord token.
- Opt-in (higher false-positive risk): phone numbers and generic high-entropy secrets.

**Allowlist and configuration**
- The page documents no config file. Allowlisting is done with `--ignore` on the CLI or `.ignore()` and `.ignore_list()` in the library.

content.content:
**License:** MIT OR Apache-2.0 for the CLI and core library. The PolyForm license no longer applies to v0.1.9 and later. Advanced team features such as `cleansh profiles sync` are inactive stubs in the open-source CLI.

**Repository:** github.com/KarmaYama/cleansh-workspace

**Install:**
- Prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases (recommended)
- `cargo install cleansh`
- From source: clone the repo, then run `cargo build --release`

**CLI commands:**
- `cleansh sanitize`: redacts input from stdin or files
- `cleansh scan`: audits input for secrets without modifying it, with exit codes for CI/CD
- `cleansh profiles`: manages local rule configurations

**Example usage:**
```
echo "My email is test@example.com" | cleansh sanitize
cat unknown_logs.txt | cleansh sanitize --engine entropy
cat build.log | cleansh scan --fail-over-threshold 0
git config --list | cleansh sanitize -c
cat error.log | cleansh sanitize -d
cleansh sanitize --enable "uk_nino,aws_secret_key" --disable "email"
```

**Flags mentioned:**
- `--engine entropy`: enables the opt-in entropy engine
- `--fail-over-threshold`: sets the scan failure threshold
- `-c`: copies output to the clipboard
- `-d`: shows a diff view
- `--config`: loads custom regex rules from YAML
- `--enable` / `--disable`: toggles rules by name

**Detected patterns:**
- Emails
- IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
- JWTs
- GitHub PATs
- Stripe keys
- AWS, GCP, and Azure cloud keys
- SSH keys and generic hex/tokens
- Credit card numbers
- US SSNs, UK NINOs, and South African IDs
- File paths (for example, `/home/user` becomes `~/`)
- Secrets with no known format, via the entropy engine

**Version and date:** 0.1.11, released 2025-12-20

**Network access and telemetry:** The page does not say whether the CLI makes network requests or collects telemetry. It describes the tool as local-only, but it does not give details on network behavior.

content.text:
I recommend **leakguard**. It's a free Rust command-line tool, MIT/Apache-2.0 licensed, that reads from stdin or files and writes the scrubbed text to stdout. It comes with detectors already built in, so you don't write any regexes. Version 1.0.0 came out on 2026-10-06.

**What it catches by default:** email addresses, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, JWTs, AWS access keys, credentials inside URLs (`user:pass@host`), and keys or tokens from GitHub, Slack, Stripe, Google API, OpenAI, Telegram and Discord. It also catches PEM private keys, Azure storage connection strings, MAC addresses, credit cards, IBANs and US Social Security numbers. You can turn on phone numbers and a generic high-entropy secret detector too, but they're off by default because they flag more harmless text by mistake.

**Assumption:** you can install a Rust toolchain. I only found `cargo install` as the documented install method and didn't confirm whether prebuilt binaries exist. I haven't installed or run leakguard myself; everything here comes from its published docs.

### Install
```bash
# If you don't have Rust yet: use your distro's package (e.g. `sudo apt install cargo`),
# or rustup from https://rustup.rs (read the script before you run it)
cargo install leakguard        # puts the binary in ~/.cargo/bin
leakguard --list-kinds         # checks the install and lists the detector names
```

### First run
```bash
# 1. Make a test file and look at the result
printf 'user=alice@corp.com from 10.1.2.3 key=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE\n' | leakguard

# 2. Scrub a real log before pasting it
leakguard server.log > server.clean.log
# or pipe it:
journalctl -u myapp --since "1 hour ago" | leakguard > clean.txt

# 3. Copy straight to the clipboard (X11 shown; use wl-copy on Wayland)
leakguard server.log | xclip -selection clipboard
```

### Options worth knowing
- `--stats` shows how many items of each type were redacted, so you can check that it actually caught things.
- `--check` exits with status 1 if it finds anything. You can use it as a gate before sharing a file.
- `--redact-word AcmeCorp` and `--redact-literal "db-prod-01:HOST"` hide your own sensitive terms, like internal hostnames, customer names or usernames. **No built-in detector covers those.**
- `--ignore 127.0.0.1,noreply@example.com` leaves harmless values alone.
- `--mask partial --keep 4` keeps the last 4 characters, which helps you tell redacted values apart when debugging.
- `--only email,ipv4` and `--without <kind>` limit which detectors run.

### Alternatives
- **[cleansh](https://docs.rs/crate/cleansh/latest)** (Rust, MIT/Apache-2.0): `cat app.log | cleansh sanitize`. It has an optional entropy-based engine for secrets with no known format (`--engine entropy`), copies to the clipboard with `-c`, shows a diff with `-d`, and loads custom rules from YAML. It's a good second choice. The docs call it local-only but don't say anything specific about network access or telemetry.
- **[hexredact](https://github.com/happygream/hexredact)**: does reversible redaction. The same value always gets the same placeholder, and it saves a mapping file, so you can match the AI's answer back to the real hosts and IPs.
- **[local-redact](https://github.com/sumankrsh/local-redact)** (Python): `cat app.log | local-redact redact`, with an allowlist and a JSON report.

### Limitations
These tools all match patterns. They miss secrets that don't look like any known format, such as plain passwords in config dumps, session cookies or custom tokens. Unless you add them with `--redact-word`, they also miss internal domain names, usernames and file paths. Skim the output, or the `--stats` summary, before you paste.

I also checked pickfit's catalog of tested tools, but it had nothing that does this job. These picks came from a web search instead.

Sources:
- [leakguard on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/latest) · [leakguard binary source](https://docs.rs/crate/leakguard/latest/source/src/bin/leakguard.rs) · repo: https://github.com/ptukovar/leakguard
- [cleansh on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/cleansh/latest) · [cleansh crate docs](https://docs.rs/cleansh/0.1.7/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/cleansh/)
- [hexredact](https://github.com/happygream/hexredact)
- [local-redact](https://github.com/sumankrsh/local-redact)
- [rog7/redact](https://github.com/rog7/redact)
